prior_importants.description: SKILL.md and LOOP.md still show `pup answer <session> <n>` / `pup answer conductor …` without the now-required `--question <id>`, so a copied command fails with commander's 'required option not specified'.

findings.description: A conductor started before this change has no PUP_CONDUCTOR_RUN in its tmux server, so after an upgrade (or a pulled branch under `pnpm dev`) every `pup conductor ask` it runs is refused as if the caller were an impostor and its earlier question vanishes from the inbox; when the server holds no token but a conductor window exists, the refusal could say to restart it with `pup conductor start`.

The call-site comment on minting the run token ("Minted per start and kept in the window alone: what seals this run's questions…") restates the JSDoc on `ConductorLaunchOptions.run` in session-runtime.service.ts; general.md §Comments says a call-site copy of the callee's docs is deleted.

The comment "Not `-e`: tmux's argv is in every user's `ps`." restates the `ClaudeWindowOptions.serverEnv` JSDoc this PR added ("through the client's environment rather than its argv"); general.md §Comments says the explanation lives at the seam, so delete the call-site copy.

`sameText` wraps `timingSafeEqual` for a constant-time compare, but the PR's own threat model says any same-user caller who could time the comparison can read the token outright with `show-environment`/`ps -E`; plain `===` on the two hex strings would drop the helper, the import and the Buffer allocations unless a caller who can time but not read is named.

What the seal does not stop is written out in full in the `openConductorQuestion` JSDoc, the `conductorRun` JSDoc (session-runtime.service.ts ~297-307) and ADR 93, so a change to the trust model has three copies to keep in step; a one-line contract pointing at decision 93 in each JSDoc would leave the ADR as the single source.

process_issues.description: Reviewer did not read testing.md, the changed test files' diffs, or the ADR 93 diff, so the testing-convention and ADR-compliance checks on this PR were not done.

Reviewer covered the tmux, commander and HTTP form surfaces, but not the node:crypto HMAC code in conductor.service.ts, the dashboard service/overview changes, or the ADR 93 cross-check against other design docs.
The non-test source diff was truncated on read, so the reviewer checked it with targeted greps and did not read src/cli/ui/* or src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts for forbidden patterns.
Dropped one docs nit (markConductorQuestion's JSDoc documents a return value with no consumer): it named no cost or reader misled, so it fails the finding bar.
